case_type: Criminal Appeal / Murder Reference / PSL Application

facts.location: Civil Hospital and surrounding area, Tandlianwala, Faisalabad
facts.summary: The appellant Usman allegedly shot deceased Mukhtar Ahmad and injured Muhammad Imran during a land dispute altercation. Eyewitnesses were cited, but their reliability was questioned.

legal_issues.finding: Unexplained delay in FIR registration and postmortem weakened prosecution case.
Eyewitnesses were chance witnesses; statements contained dishonest improvements; ocular account not reliable.
Medical evidence corroborates injury but cannot identify assailant.
No independent evidence substantiated alleged motive; motive considered immaterial for conviction.
Parcel containing firearm and bullets lacked proper custody; PFSA report unreliable.
Multiple doubts in ocular account, medical evidence, and recovery entitle appellant to acquittal.
Judgment of acquittal not perverse or arbitrary; protected by double presumption of innocence.

appellant: Delay in FIR; chance witnesses; dishonest improvements; medical evidence cannot establish identity; compromised forensic evidence; motive not proven; benefit of doubt applies.
respondent: FIR registered; witnesses and medical evidence provided; firearm recovery and PFSA report support prosecution; motive exists due to land dispute.

judgment_summary.Criminal Appeal No.81797-J of 2022: Allowed; appellant Usman acquitted; prior conviction and sentences set aside
judgment_summary.Murder Reference No.23 of 2023: Answered in Negative; death sentence not confirmed
judgment_summary.release_of_appellants: Forthwith, if not required in any other case

legal_references.case_name: Mst. ASIA BIBI v. The STATE
HAJI PAIO KHAN v. SHER BIAZ
MUHAMMAD SHAFI alias KHDDOO v. The STATE

remarks: Due to unexplained FIR delay, unreliable eyewitnesses, dishonest improvements, compromised forensic evidence, and unproven motive, the appellant Usman is acquitted and prior convictions are set aside.
